findings.title: Repository-controlled links can redirect run-state writes outside the repository
findings.description: RunDirectory validates only the textual run ID and then combines it with runsPath. It does not verify that `.quality`, `runs`, or the selected run directory is free of symbolic links, junctions, or other reparse points, nor that the resolved destination remains beneath the repository root. If repository contents are attacker-controlled, a pre-existing link can cause Create, AppendProgress, WriteStatus, WriteResult, or WriteObservation to create or overwrite files outside the repository using the service account's privileges.
findings.recommendation: Prefer storing orchestration state outside repositories that may contain untrusted content. Otherwise, resolve and validate every existing path component, reject symbolic links/junctions/reparse points, verify the final resolved path remains under a trusted canonical root, and use platform-supported no-follow or directory-handle-relative file operations to avoid check-to-use races.

findings.title: Unbounded persisted JSON can exhaust process memory
findings.description: Required run artifacts are read completely into a string and deserialized without enforcing a file-size limit. An attacker able to supply or modify repository contents can place an oversized manifest or status file under `.quality/runs`, causing LoadAll to allocate memory proportional to attacker-controlled input and potentially terminate or severely degrade the API process. The surrounding exception handling does not mitigate memory exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Enforce conservative maximum sizes before reading run artifacts, deserialize from a bounded stream, cap collection and string lengths where practical, and reject oversized files with a controlled load failure.
